reviews.text: Dr. Cohen is an angel!
Matilda, thank you for the 5-star rating! We truly appreciate your support and trust in our team. 🐾 …

I absolutely love the way the surgeon Dr. Donchik and the vet techs were beyond sweet and kind! They answered all the questions and never once made me feel as if i was annoying them. My experience with them was amazing and they took such great care of my dog! While they were great, the receptionists are absolutely terrible. They are so rude and unwelcoming. In particular Juliana. She had a terrible attitude, she gives owners dirty looks, she talks to people terribly. she talks horribly about people after the call for questions and is very dismissive. She needs better training in customer service. Other than that my entire experience was other wise very well!
Very nice staff. Always available when I have an emergency. Even throught text messege with the doctor. Thank you for helping my babies.

It has taken me a while to write this…I can’t express enough gratitude for the love and kindness my family and I received here. We ended up meeting near the end of our dog’s life and how I wish I had been there sooner.

From booking the appointment, to our first visit with Dr. Aanonsen, and then several appointments with Dr. Candrilli, we received nothing short of kindness and care for our angel Freddy. The entire team wanted the best for him and truly cared for his comfort in his final months, even though we didn’t know or accept it was actually his final few months.

I know how broken I was when having the conversation to let Freddy go over the rainbow bridge, and really only now am I processing how heavy and devastating that must be—to be faced with so often in this field. Dr. Candrilli was kind and emotional in the moment, and though she only knew Freddy briefly, you wouldn’t have known that wish how she held him at our last visit.

I highly recommend Bay Street Animal hospital for the care and health of your animals.
Anne, thank you for the 5-star rating! We truly appreciate your support and trust in our team. 🐾 …

Anyone who writes a 5 star review is lying. Since they expanded they’ve been rude and entitled. Call and try a make an appointment and you're on hold FOREVER. Maybe hire more staff?!? They’ll pick up the phone and don’t even know who they’re talking to. Brought my cat in and there were 2 roaches climbing the walls while I waited

We've taken my dog here for years, but I regret ever using this place. They basically charge you as soon as you walk through the door, it cost and arm and a leg to have your pet taken care of. They just want your money and they know what you'll pay to save your dog or cat but there's is no guarantee they will. My dog Paddy recently got sick with an autoimmune disease, they kept him in the hospital for a week, it costed over 4 thousand dollars and he only lived maybe 2 weeks later and sadly passed on Nov 7th 2024. So what did they actually do? My poor dog is gone and they just got richer. Everyone at my local park has something bad to say about this place as well. If I ever get a new dog in the future after my mom and I have had time to heal from our massive loss, we will not be coming back to these thieves. They don't care about your pets.

They overrode my informed consent.
Declining a follow-up test was my decision to make, and instead of respecting it, they withheld my cat’s medication to force me to come in on their timeline instead of mine. After years of being happy here, this was genuinely disappointing.

I would not recommend Bay Street Animal Hospital for end of life services. One memorial item had apparently been sitting at the office the entire time, yet nobody contacted her.

The lack of communication, compassion, and accountability during such a difficult time was incredibly disappointing. No grieving pet owner should have to chase down memorial items for their beloved pet. Rose and her family deserved much better.

Dr Steve is the best vet around . We drive 3 hours each way from ct  just to be in good hands .

Excellent compassionate staff, receptionist and expert services.  Fast diagnosis & remedies.  #sirdayz_thecat loves them.
His pancreatitis treatment worked perfectly. It was cured in two days at the hospital. We noted that he had stopped eating, did a little Googling, and got him to the Vet for tests. All his blood work showed him perfect. Then when appetite enhancer medicines only had short term results, further tests determined the cause. He is now back to normal, very energetic and very happy to be home.

I had already placed my review and want to wholeheartedly thank Dr.Justine Candrilli for her professionalism, kindness, compassion and very positive adjective that i can think of when we brought our cat Jake due to complications from bladder cancer. She helped us make a difficult decision based on her informative prognosis. Myself and my wife will always remember her as the most caring Veterinarian that we ever met. She is an asset to her profession and the company she works for. The good Lord has made wonderful people and she is definitely one of them helping us during this most difficult time. Thank you Dr. Justine Candrilli, you will always have a special place in our hearts and wish you well throughout your entire life. Thank you Bay St hospital  also for providing us with kind and compassionate technicians during this most difficult time.

Unsanitary Conditions, Illness, and Unnecessary Charges

I’ve been coming here for about a year, but after this experience I will not be returning.
When I picked up my two puppies after their spay surgery (March 7), there was dog feces on the floor. The receptionist went and got a wet mop, no bucket wiped the feces with the wet mop only no disinfectant, no proper cleaning, and then walked away with the wet mop dripping and came back with a wet floor sign. No one came back to sanitize the area, I was there for over 10 minutes after. This is completely unacceptable for a medical facility.

Less than 24 hours after bringing my puppies home (they were there March 5th-March7th), both were sneezing, and one had serious breathing issues. I brought this to their attention and was told it could be “allergies,” which I strongly disagree with.

I took her in and ended up paying $139 the appoint and for antibiotics and allergy medication because I was concerned about my puppy’s breathing.

This felt completely avoidable given the unsanitary conditions I witnessed.

I trusted this place with my pets, but after seeing how basic sanitation is handled, and also they did not take accountability for my dogs getting sick.  I no longer feel comfortable bringing them here.

If I could give this place ZERO stars, I would. The one star goes to Dr. Cohen for always being kind and more importantly, knowledgeable of his craft.

Unfortunately, my experiences with Dr. Cavallaro were extremely concerning. She diagnosed my pitbull mix with degenerative myelopathy (DM) based only on a physical exam, without recommending any imaging. Months later, a neurologist at Red Bank Veterinary Hospital correctly diagnosed my dog (via MRI) with a meningioma and said they were “appalled” by how the initial diagnosis was made.

Because I trusted that initial (mis)diagnosis, on my own accord, I spent months providing hydrotherapy to my girl instead of getting the critical care she truly needed. It was the Dr treating her for hydrotherapy that questioned the DM diagnosis and suggested I get an MRI at Red Bank.

In a separate incident (during the time my pittie was getting hydrotherapy) Dr Cavallaro administered an antibiotic to my senior dog that was contraindicated for her condition—without my consent! When I pointed this out, there was no acknowledgment, no apology—nothing! Administering medication without owner consent, especially when the owner is present, is both unethical and unacceptable. It also demonstrated a failure to review my dog’s medical history.

After that experience, I never returned. She’s fortunate I did not report her to the New York State Office of the Professions, which handles misconduct for veterinarians.

Both of my dogs have since passed, and while these events occurred a few years ago, this review is long overdue. I trusted this practice with animals I loved deeply, and those experiences had lasting consequences.

What an amazing experience from beginning to end! The entire visit was quick and efficient! I was in and out within an hour, which made everything so much easier. Samantha at the front desk was so nice and welcoming and very helpful from the moment I walked in. Dr. Justin Arleo was fantastic, so gentle, patient, and caring with my pup, which I really appreciated. The whole staff made the experience smooth and stress-free. I highly recommend Bay Street Animal Hospital to anyone looking for compassionate and professional care for their pets!!

Today we had to say goodbye to our dog Brownie after 16 years and 6 months of being part of our family. Anyone who has loved a dog knows how heartbreaking that moment is.

Dr. Robert Cohen and the staff at Bay Street Animal Hospital showed our family a level of compassion and humanity that we will never forget. Dr. Cohen took the time to walk us through Brownie’s condition and helped us understand that we were facing the final stage of his life. He spoke with honesty, patience, and kindness, which made an incredibly painful decision a little easier to carry.

When it came time to let Brownie go, they treated him with dignity and gave our family the space to be with him and say goodbye. There was no rushing, no coldness, just genuine care for both our dog and our family.

Sixteen and a half years is a lifetime of memories, and while today was one of the hardest days we’ve had, we are grateful that Dr. Cohen and the team at Bay Street Animal Hospital helped us through it with such compassion.

If you ever find yourself in the difficult position of needing care for a beloved pet, you want people around you who truly understand that animals are family. Today, Dr. Cohen and his team showed that they do.
Thank you for the 5 stars!

Well I felt like I didn't really get much attention when I got there they took my cat in the back I wasn't allowed to go he came back about an hour later to gave me four different medicines I did ask him if they can cut his nails they said they couldn't I just didn't feel like they paid much attention to me somebody came out spoke to me briefly I guess that was the doctor he said that it looks like a UTI and I was the last time I saw him and a half an hour later some young gentleman came out I guess he was a tech he gave me the medicine and I was it they gave me all capsules and pills which was totally impossible to give to him so when I got home I called them back and I said no no you have to give me liquid form they said we'll let him know nobody ever call me back The next morning I called again they said well he should be in shortly the doctor Will your message is in the file then I called back again maybe about two 3 hours later I says he's been in why can't he give me 5 minutes of his time finally by my fourth call about 10 minutes later he called me back and I explain to him that you got I noticed stuff comes in liquid form so I can't say that I was happy with the visit I've been there before cuz I have another cat that I took there but something must have changed over there and I didn't care for the service

I give this place ZERO stars! I had a heartbreaking experience here and would strongly urge others to stay away from this joke of a hospital.

I brought my kitten in because he was sick. Within about 20 minutes of arriving, he was gone. I understand he was already ill, but what made this even worse was how he was handled. I watched staff treat my tiny kitten with what felt like roughness and a complete lack of compassion. Their communication with me was cold and lacked empathy at a moment when kindness mattered most.

My kitten was already fragile, and the added stress of being restrained and handled the way he was only seemed to make things worse. He went into cardiac arrest. I was told they performed three rounds of CPR, but when they returned him to me, it did not look like CPR had been done. I left feeling sick with guilt that I brought him here for care and that I wasn’t allowed to stay close to him during testing and care—something I believe could have reduced his fear and stress and he would still be with me today.

What I will never forget is that after handing me my kitten’s body, they asked me to settle the bill. That moment felt unbelievably insensitive and cruel.

The veterinarian mentioned having 10 years of experience, but based on what I witnessed, I did not feel my kitten received the careful, gentle, compassionate treatment he needed.

This was traumatizing and devastating. I would not recommend this hospital to anyone who wants their pet treated with empathy, gentleness, and respect—especially in an emergency.

Absolutely disgraceful, predatory, and heartless

This place should be ashamed to call itself a veterinary hospital. In my experience, the staff here showed staggering levels of greed, indifference, and lack of basic compassion toward both pets and their owners. When you walk in scared and vulnerable, worried about an animal you love, they don’t see a patient — they see a credit card.

The way they operate feels borderline fraudulent: vague explanations, pressure tactics, and inflated charges presented as “urgent” with little transparency. Questions are brushed off, alternatives are barely discussed, and you’re made to feel guilty or irresponsible if you hesitate to agree to whatever outrageously priced service they push next.

What’s most disturbing is the cold, dismissive, almost cruel attitude toward animals clearly in distress and owners who are emotional and scared. There is zero empathy here. No reassurance. No kindness. Just transactional, rushed interactions that make it painfully clear this is about money, not care.

Veterinary medicine should be rooted in trust and compassion. This place embodies the opposite - money-hungry, callous, and predatory. If you actually love your pet and want them treated with dignity by people who give a damn, go literally anywhere else.

I deeply regret bringing my pet here, and I would never recommend this hospital to anyone.

BAY STREET ANIMAL HOSPITAL did a fantastic job with my cat Teddy Nemo. Teddy had been crying alot and struggling to go to the bathroom. I had no idea what to do, I was very stressed out! I made a few calls, and found Bay Street Animal Hospital, 999 Bay Street, Staten Island. They said they take walk-ins (emergency situations get seen immediately).  The walk-in price is $150 to get full check-up. They reported they are open 24/7. I was RELIEVED to hear all of that, PLUS the kind person with whom I spoke-- SAMANTHA-- really made me feel LESS stressed. She was kind and welcoming when Teddy Nemo and I walked in. It is SO important to get COMPASSIONATE helpful staff at the front desk!! Thank you Samantha ❤️.   Next we were greeted by Andre--- SO pleasant and helpful and very understanding when I said I was so worried about Teddy!  Then Dr. Arleo came in to do a thorough check up on Teddy. Overall, I loved the way they treated me and Teddy. Consummate Professionals, very knowledgeable, accommodating, excellent listening skills. Dr. Arleo was super kind, empathetic, helpful, and understood my financial concerns. I am profoundly GRATEFUL to everyone at Bay Street Animal Hospital and I will not forget how kind & wonderful they treated me & my cat, Teddy. A thousand THANK YOUs to all of you!
-- Cynthia Monares, Staten Island, NY 10301
Thank you for the 5 stars!

If I could give a 0 star, I would.
These people that I have dealt with are absolute savages with no compassion.
This practice does not care for the animals/pets or their owners, only for your hard earned cash.
Karma will deal with you, trust.

They refused to tell me the price of the bloodwork and a minor procedure that was "required" for said procedure(which is confirmed false by multiple other vet places and ASPCA).
They also did tests and other stuff that I did not consent to or was aware of, I was informed only after everything was done.
For example, their reason for administrating the FIV test (without our consent) is to “protect my staff”, what a load of bs, FIV cannot be transmitted through humans, and the vet even complimented my cat’s gentle personality and docile demeanor.
They definitely pick and choose who to target.

Avoid this place at all cost, there are way better options on the island or in Brooklyn.

I cannot say enough wonderful things about Bay Street Animal Hospital. From the moment you walk in, you feel genuinely cared for — both as a pet parent and for your pet.

Samantha at the front desk is always kind, patient, and incredibly helpful. She makes scheduling, check-ins, and questions feel easy and stress-free, which means so much when you’re worried about your fur baby.

The vet techs, Kourtni and Angel, are absolutely amazing. They are gentle, knowledgeable, and clearly love what they do. They take the time to explain everything, make sure your pet is comfortable, and treat them like their own.

And Dr. Arleo, who takes care of my dog Vader, is outstanding. He is thorough, compassionate, and takes the time to truly listen and explain all options. I never feel rushed, and I always feel confident that Vader is receiving the best care possible.

This entire team goes above and beyond, and it shows in every interaction. I’m so grateful to have found a veterinary hospital I completely trust. Highly recommend Bay Street Animal Hospital to anyone looking for exceptional care for their pets.
Dr Cavallaro is the most knowledgeable, professional and courteous. She has been taking care of my dogs for the better part of 35 years. She is the best.

We took our 10-year-old Standard Schnauzer, Benny, to this clinic for the first time after noticing he was having issues. We had nothing but a great experience with every staff member we met, and our pet was treated with genuine kindness and professionalism.
As for Dr. Cohen, he went above and beyond to find a solution to Benny's health problem. The clinic is also well-equipped with X-Ray, CT, a diagnostic lab, etc. We highly recommend this clinic to anyone looking for compassionate, high-quality veterinary care.
Thank you for the 5 stars! We love caring for your pets!

They helped me through a very tough decision. I had put my cat Mamaz down due to an illness that she didn't recover from.  Their staff is one of the best that I have seen in a long time.  If you live on Staten Island, take your pets. Their prices are not expensive and the quality of service is amazing

I am so thankful for everyone at Bay Street Animal Hospital. They were so great with my senior dog Zada. She was on the point of death and now she is thriving more than a month later. I thank God for them all. I cannot recommend them more highly

I was very upset that my French Bulldog was not feeling well at all, I went here because it was close to were I live

They were very careful an caring when handling my dog

They ran test showed me what was wrong an gave me medicine an care instructions for my dog

The next morning she woke up almost herself an the following day pretty much normal

I thought the bill was going to significant but to my surprise it was lower than I thought

For me it was a good experience, the Veterinarian wasn't over friendly but he got right to the point an when he saw how upset I was with my dogs condition he offered me his cellphone to call if any issues should arise to me that was very comforting that I wasn't an ATM machine...

I have used Bay Street animal hospital since I moved into the URBY over 3 years ago.  I am a quadriplegic on strong medication one day a pill fell on the floor and my puppy Bella found it.  She almost died and the vets there saved her life!  I am forever grateful to them! I now have a second puppy and they are the only vet I would ever think of bringing him to!

Never again.

My dog was prescribed thyroid medication.

After approximately 3 to 4 weeks he began experiencing increased nighttime restlessness, including prolonged pacing and inability to sleep.

For several nights in a row, no one in my household slept.

I contacted the clinic and spoke with the attending veterinarian seeking a solution.

No medication adjustments, no alternatives, no guidance. I was just handed an updated bloodwork results and told by an assistant to continue giving my dog the same medication with nothing directly communicated by the veterinarian.

I am super disappointed with the veterinarian I saw that day and found the interaction very disingenuous and dismissive.

Staten Island pet owners, please strongly consider going elsewhere. Do not expect clear communication or meaningful follow-up from this hospital.

4 visits, over $500 and a lot of attitude from vet to treat two sneezing kittens.. Now having to wait 4 days for a SOAP note to take my pet to a new vet because the vet "didn't complete her notes" extremely unprofessional and careless

I took my 3 yr old cat in tonight, I was treated with respect, kindness and understanding. My baby was immediately taken in for a better look, I already suspected it was a blockage from what I read but I’ve never had a cat with one before. My heart was breaking and they calmly went through the list of what would be needed to treat him, once the bloodwork came back (less then 30-40min wait) for all the results we knew we needed to be aggressive about treatment. I got a phone call 30 mins ago from the vet telling me my baby is feeling much relief and they were able to catheterize and release urine and they are pushing fluids and helping him🥹🥹 that phone call was above and beyond. I can’t wait to have my baby back home. Thank you to the whole staff tonight for being so kind. -Cole and Katie

Me & my bf have been going to this facility for years with our dog Roxy. Everyone has always been good, but Dr. Aleo & vet tech Olivia were phenomenal!! Roxy has such bad vet anxiety & they were so gently with her. I’ve never seen our dog so calm with these visits. They were very informative and helpful. I can never thank them enough for how good they were with our baby Roxy! Receptionist Gabriella was also VERY sweet over the phone as I am a office manager. She had great customer service. We can’t thank you all 3 enough ❤️

We lost our family cat in a freak accident on Thanksgiving day. The wonderful staff stayed open later for us, gave us the time and space we needed to say goodbye, and were so kind and empathetic during such a difficult time.  ❤️ We can not thank them enough and will continue to take our future pets here. 🌈🙏🏽 …
Thanks for the review, Isaac! Our team appreciates it.

Bought in my cat for a wellness check up was quoted a little under $350 over the phone for a check up and bloodwork. I left with a bill of over $700 because the vet ordered X-rays saying she suspected a bladder issue. How? His bloodwork came back clean and has had no issues urinating. Only for the diagnosis to be a perfectly healthy cat who was constipated. For that I was offered hospitalization and an enema as treatment versus first prescribing medication to help him use the bathroom. What a joke. For others, be warned they are not transparent about their pricing until you reach the front desk and pricing is not displayed anywhere. I suggest asking directly as they “recommend” additional tests or treatments. I used to go to Park Slope Veterinary and this place is even more expensive which is ludicrous.
Using them for our fur babies for 20 yrs
Writing this months later but, Dr. Bob saved my cat and I couldn’t be more grateful for him and his team. Very knowledgeable and compassionate, they even send sweet note cards. Love this place

After putting my cat - my best boy of 12 years - to sleep a few weeks ago, I went in to pick up his paw prints. Turns out they "lost" his prints. It was nice seeing everyone else's beloved pet's envelopes of fur/prints in the pile. I'm absolutely gutted.

We bring our four pets there, the workers are unbelievably friendly and love our pets. The veterans Are thorough, they explained everything in layman's terms. We also boarded our dogs there for a week had no issues.
Staff is excellent. Vets are very knowledgeable and caring.

We are beyond grateful to Dr. Donchik and the incredible team at Bay Street Animal Hospital for saving our Booboo’s life. When others told us there was nothing they could do, Dr. Donchik refused to give up. He performed a complex surgery that no other doctor was willing to attempt — and because of his skill, compassion, and determination, our dog is still with us today.

The entire staff went above and beyond for us — treating our dog with love, patience, and care as if he were their own. Their kindness and professionalism gave us hope during one of the hardest times of our lives.

There are truly no words to express how thankful we are. Dr. Donchik didn’t just perform a surgery — he gave our family more time with our best friend, and we will never forget that. 🐾💙
Thank you for the 5 stars!
They saved my Riley Roo’s life — I could never thank them enough
Thank you for the 5 stars!

They just don’t really show you the type of compassion you would expect when people choose a profession working around animals and pets so just be conscious about that when choosing to go to this place. I had a terrible experience in my house seeing my cat dying cause he is old so out of panic I came to this place and I guess that’s my fault cause I was looking to just get help for my cat but soon as they took them to the back and I had a chance in talking with 1 doctor and a receptionist and before my cat could be seen they were looking to get over 500$ with out even saying anything just for the visit and blood work. Not the price but how the energy was in there gave me a bad feeling in my gut when I didn’t know what decision to make and just was unsure and wanted some more info and they got snappy and was like “I guess you just want your cat back cause that’s what it looks like you are leaning towards” and also said “ok let’s not get off topic here” about me just asking basic questions. good thing I trusted my gut cause soon as I got home my cat Boots had passed away in my mothers arms after they rejected him and sent me out the door. My mother even asked them what can we do or if they can give any advice and the worker said “he can’t disclose or say anything due to us not following through” Everyone’s experience is different but this place made me feel awful at a low point in my life and I don’t wish bad upon the people who work there but this place needs to close down. Turning away dying animals and not giving feedback or advice in how to care for them if someone can’t afford your price is inhumane. We need a place that has people who love animals and are soft spoken and are well trained to deal with grieving ppl having to put there animaIs down. I rather my cat pass away home then in that place around ppl he didn’t know anyway.

DO NOT BRING YOUR DOG HERE UNLESS YOU WANT TO HAVE A LIFETIME OF ISSUES FOR YOUR PET or even death! I BROUGHT MY DOG FOR HIS ROUTINE ALLERGY MEDS. THEY FIRST TOLD ME HE IS DUE FOR HIS RABBIES VACCINE BECAUSE ITS Mandatory. He had bad reactions to vaccines in the past which they should know of bc its in his records, but I felt threatened so I said ok. Then without asking me or explaining to me they gave him a shot called Cytopoint. I found out when I got the bill. Well after that his paws blew up and he began to itch severely. Then he broke out in horrible rashes all over his body. This also went to his eyes and his eyes began to leak and cloud over. Thousands of dollars later and multiple vet visits by specials he still has a severe issue. Been on strong medications ever since. He may lose his eyes. The specialist told me he may have developed an autoimmune disease and will need to be on meds for the rest of his life. Plus his blood work showed severe inflammation and infection. Whatever they did (probably combo of both) did my dog in. Cytopoint is deadly. I looked into this and so many people have stories of their dogs dying or developing an autoimmune disease due to the Cytopoint shot. Especially in smaller dogs. This place should be ashamed. They only care about money. Didn't look at my dogs history or explain anything before they gave him this shot. After all this I may have to put my dog down. He's still in horrible shape and I have no more money left.
**Update: my dog ended up passing due to their negligence. I pray this place gets shut down!

Took my cat Bella there. Staff was great and worked within my budget to help. Yes, certain tests and procedures cost money, just as it does with a human. Thank you guys for working with me to afford care for my Bella.

Horrible practice. Please do yourself and your pet the biggest favor and go elsewhere. I lost my beloved dog of 13 years because Dr. Cohen was not giving him the correct dose of insulin (an extremely low amount). I suspect this was so my dog would continue to be in and out of the hospital, which equals more money (we paid over $10,000). When my sister brought our dog in for the last time, she had questions regarding his treatment, to which she was met with hostility and yelling by Dr. Cohen. She was told, “Your dog is not going to make it anyway and will die.” I would not be shocked if my dog was being neglected while being an inpatient. The times that I visited him, he seemed more and more lethargic due to the incorrect insulin dosage. For scale, I know dogs his size that get 7ml of insulin. My dog was only getting 0.5 -1ml once a day! If you love your pets, please bring them somewhere else that will care for them like family instead of this practice that is money hungry and will keep your dog sick to maximize profit.

I've been going here since they opened years ago. Dr. Cavellaro is simply the best. She cares, she listens and has been spot on with her diagnoses. The staff is always friendly and helpful. Bianca was there and helped me during a crucial emergency.
I recommend them highly!
Thank you for your review!
Doctors, techs and staff are friendly, helpful and seem to genuinely care for all of their animals. My dogs are in great hands.
Thank you for your review!
Thank you for your review!
Dr. Cohen and all of the other doctors are not only competent and thorough, but actually CARE. Highly recommend!

I’ve taken every single one of my dogs here. They’ve treated my dogs through pneumonia, cancer, and an attack by another dog. One of my dogs is alive now because of this vet hospital. The staff has always been excellent, knowledgeable and kind. Even when the news isn’t what I wanted, they always approached m and my pets with sensitivity. There isn’t a better vet practice on Staten Island. Plus it’s always clean.
Excellent service and attention.

I recently had to take my cat in for emergency care, and I arrived at Bay Street Animal Hospital visibly distressed, holding him in my arms and in tears. The moment I approached the front desk, I was immediately told the walk-in cost, before any concern or compassion was shown for my situation. When I gave my cat’s name, the staff member laughed, which felt incredibly inappropriate given the circumstances.

There was a clear lack of empathy from the start. The staff focused more on the cost of services than on what care my pet would receive. The $150 exam fee was not explained, and one staff member even told me to expect to spend $1,000.

When they took my cat to the back, I asked if I could accompany him and was told no. When he was brought back, no one explained what was done or what was found. I asked for clarification, visibly upset, and instead of addressing my concerns, the person at the desk picked up the phone while I was speaking through tears. I took my dog here with a clear bowel obstruction. The survival rate of this condition for canines is between 83-99%. I pay for pet insurance and consented to all tests including lab work and x-rays. My dog showed signs of clear internal bleeding (bloated stomach, high platelet production, low potassium and sodium, a small knot in the small intestine via xray) as well as numerous symptoms (no appetite -- he was a lab, excessive thirst, extreme lethargy, no bowel movements in the last day). I was told to come back the next day. My request (I am in healthcare) for the dog to be admitted and given saline was denied. The vet's (Stora, Candrilli) told me to give him levothyroxine after I said wouldn't eat anything including prosciutto and the vets words were to 'try a hamburger' and figure it out myself.

My dog died the next day. I am so upset that I spend the last 12 hours of my dogs life force feeding him with my bear hands. When my dog went incontinent that morning, I rushed him to the vet, but he passed less than an hour later. They give me about 5 minutes to mourn (my wife was still crying) before coming back in and chasing me to pay the bill despite the fact that I've been a regular here for four years and never once had a payment issue. They then took over 6 months to return the cremated remains of my dog during which time I said nothing bad about this place.

This entire experience was emotionally devastating. The lack of urgency, compassion, and professionalism at this clinic is unforgivable. I trusted them with my dog’s life, and they failed him—and me—at every step. I strongly urge anyone considering this clinic to look elsewhere. Your pet deserves better care than what I experienced here.
